draft.title: Reading survey reports critically
card: A survey gives an estimate of a mean or median for a whole group. The estimate is only as good as the survey behind it.
Who was asked
the sample should represent the whole group. If only one kind of person is asked, the result may not match everyone.
How many
a very small sample can give a result far from the true value. A larger sample is usually more reliable, if it is chosen well.
How collected
check the questions and the method. Leading questions or people choosing whether to reply can distort the data.
draft.remember: Before trusting a survey's mean or median, ask who, how many and how.

a.q: A report says the median weekly pocket money of Year 9 students is $30. It surveyed 8 students, all from one netball team. What is the best criticism?
opts: The sample is tiny and covers only one group
The median should have been a mean
The survey asked about money, which is private
The answer of $30 is too low to be true
a.why: Eight students from one team is a small sample and may not represent all Year 9 students. Choosing a mean instead of a median is not the problem, because a survey can report either.
a.clue: Look at how many were asked and who they were.

b.q: Kai wants to estimate the mean time Year 9 students at his school spend on homework. Which survey is most trustworthy?
opts: 120 students from all Year 9 classes, same question
30 friends from his lunch group, asked in person
The first 100 students to reply to a link he posted
60 students from the school library after school
b.why: The first option asks many students from every class using one question. The 100 volunteers are a larger group, but they chose to reply, so they may not represent everyone.
b.clue: A bigger sample is not enough if the people chose themselves.

a.best: The sample is tiny and covers only one group

b.best: 120 students from all Year 9 classes, same question

problems.detail: Why (b) calls the right answer 'the first option', but the options are shown in random order, so a student may see it in a different place. Name the option by its content instead.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear answer. The only issue is that why (b) refers to 'the first option', which breaks when the options are shuffled.
